deliverable: Mandatory Data-Generation Subtask: Slack-style evidence impact demonstration
summary: Four live OpenRouter runs across two authorized opportunities and one authorization-scope A/B pair show that generated Slack-style evidence is correctly ingested, permissioned, retrieved, and ranked into the model's context on every attempt, and was extracted into a validated, cited claim by the Conversation Intelligence Agent on one attempt -- but that claim did not survive the Negotiation Strategy Agent's independent re-synthesis into the shipped Deal Brief sections. No live run produced a finalized brief with a Slack citation. This file documents the with/without retrieval-level difference and the exact pipeline stage where Slack evidence drops out, with no fabricated content.

method.withoutSlackMechanism: Ran the standard live pipeline twice, back-to-back, with only the requester's authorization scope changed between runs. For the 'without Slack' run, permission_grants row id 'grant:USR-5001:ACC-2001:slack' was updated to can_read=false directly in the slacato_samples scratch database (never the slacato or slacato_e2e databases, and never fixtures/cato/policies/access_permissions.tsv), then restored to can_read=true immediately after the run completed. packages/infrastructure/src/worker/postgres-deal-brief-workflow-services.ts calls readPermissionGrants(requestedBy, accountId) fresh at retrieval time for every run and feeds the result into authorizeOpportunity() (packages/core/src/domain/permissions/authorize.ts), so the revoked grant deterministically removed 'slack' from that run's AccessScope.sourceTypes and therefore from buildEvidencePlan's admitted source types (packages/core/src/application/evidence/retriever.ts) for that run only. This is an authorization-scope toggle on scratch data, not a fixture edit or hand-edited artifact.

withSlackAttempt1.note: Slack evidence retrieved and admitted into every specialist's context but not used in any extracted claim; this attempt's brief also had degraded quality (empty stakeholderMap and sourceEvidence, five hallucinated stakeholder names pruned by validation) unrelated to Slack.

slackClaimedBySpecialist.statement: We still need the final owner matrix and success metrics confirmed by the client stakeholders.
slackClaimedBySpecialist.validationOutcome: kept (not listed among this artifact's INSUFFICIENT_CLAIM_SUPPORT claims: claim_1, claim_4, claim_6)

withSlackAttempt2.note: The Negotiation Strategy Agent (Main agent) does not forward the Conversation Agent's claim list verbatim into buyerGoalsAndBusinessDrivers / missingInformation / negotiationState -- it re-derives its own smaller set of claims from the shared evidence pool with new claim IDs and re-written statements. In this run it selected claim_goal_1 (gong_transcript:CALL-008:transcript:0) and claim_driver_1 (gong_transcript:CALL-001:transcript:0), and did not carry claim_8 (slack:SLK-9002:0) forward. missingInformation in the final brief is populated only from claims that FAILED validation (claim_neg_2, claim_stk_1..5), so a well-supported but unselected claim like claim_8 has no path into that section either.

withoutSlackAuthorized.authorizationChange: permission_grants row 'grant:USR-5001:ACC-2001:slack' set can_read=false for the duration of this run only, then restored.
withoutSlackAuthorized.note: With Slack unauthorized, rank 13/27 (previously slack:SLK-9002:0) is filled by gong_transcript:CALL-008:transcript:2, and gong_summary:CALL-005:summary:0 enters the pool for the first time at rank 19. This is the concrete, mechanical retrieval-level difference the authorization-scope toggle produces.

secondaryOpportunityCheck.purpose: Ran on a second opportunity/persona pair (not a re-roll of OPP-1001) to check whether the drop-out pattern was specific to OPP-1001's evidence mix. It was not: Slack was retrieved and authorized but not selected by any specialist agent on this opportunity either.

crossReferenceFromShippedSamples.note: Consistent with the new runs: retrieved and authorized, dropped at the Conversation Intelligence Agent's own extraction step this time (never reached any specialist_artifacts row), never surfaced as a citation.

stages.evidence: 9 rows in fixtures/cato/slack/account_team_updates.tsv, chunked and embedded alongside every other source type.
USR-5001/USR-5002/USR-5003 all carry 'slack' in permission_grants; revoking the grant for one run deterministically removed slack from that run's retrieval pool with no other change.

In 3 of 3 with-Slack live runs, the single admitted Slack chunk (sourceLimits caps Slack at 2 per section query, and gong_transcript is uncapped) landed at rank 13-16 of ~27 with a fusion score (0.111-0.147) inside the same band as many gong_transcript entries (0.13-0.17).
included_characters for the Slack row was always its full chunk size (279-330 chars, never truncated to 0), confirmed present in the same evidence pool handed to every specialist agent.

stages.result: yes, once out of 3 with-Slack runs performed for this demonstration
stages.evidence: run_a12bd817...: Conversation Intelligence Agent emitted claim_8 (confidence 0.9) citing slack:SLK-9002:0 verbatim from the Slack row's own text.
claim_8 was not among the artifact's INSUFFICIENT_CLAIM_SUPPORT claims; pruneClaims() kept it as supported.

stages.stage: carried into the final Deal Brief
stages.result: no, in all 4 with-Slack runs observed (3 performed for this demonstration plus the pre-existing shipped OPP-1003 run)
stages.evidence: The Negotiation Strategy Agent re-synthesizes buyerGoalsAndBusinessDrivers, negotiationState, and recommendedNextActions directly from the shared evidence pool with its own new claim IDs and statements, rather than forwarding upstream specialist claims verbatim. In every observed run it selected only Salesforce/Gong-sourced claims for those sections; missingInformation is populated only from claims that FAILED validation, so a supported-but-unselected claim like claim_8 has no path into any final section either.

pipelineDiagnosis.rootCause: Volume asymmetry, not a permission or retrieval defect. buildEvidencePlan (packages/core/src/application/evidence/retriever.ts) caps slack at Math.min(input.limit, 2) per section query while leaving gong_transcript uncapped ('gong_transcript: input.limit'). For OPP-1001 this yields 18 gong_transcript chunks (84.6% of the 22,670-character evidence context) against 1 slack chunk (1.26%). The generation-model agents (Conversation Intelligence and Negotiation Strategy) are given the full pool and choose what to write about; a single short update sitting among 18 same-topic transcript chunks is a plausible candidate to be extracted at all (it was, once) but a hard one for the downstream synthesis step to prioritize over its higher-volume neighbors.
pipelineDiagnosis.whatWouldChangeThis: Raising the per-source slack cap relative to gong_transcript in buildEvidencePlan's sourceLimits, or having the Negotiation Strategy Agent's prompt explicitly require representation from every authorized source type with retrieved evidence (not just the highest-scoring cluster), would give Slack updates a materially better chance of being cited in the shipped brief without changing retrieval or permissions.

reproduction.withoutSlackCommand: Using any Postgres client against slacato_samples: update permission_grants set can_read=false where id='grant:USR-5001:ACC-2001:slack'; pnpm tsx drive.ts USR-5001 OPP-1001; then restore can_read=true
prerequisites: Source .env and override DATABASE_URL to the dedicated slacato_samples database.
Run the API and worker against the same database with SLACATO_BOOTSTRAP=1.
Approve the resulting evidence_review approval subject (category triggered by the LEGAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED warning) before the run can finalize.
Never apply the can_read toggle to the slacato or slacato_e2e databases.
